title: Crispy Grated Potato Focaccia
changes_from_base: Topped with squeezed-dry grated potato, thyme and pepper that crisps like a hash brown; no flaky salt.
summary: Focaccia under a crunchy, golden layer of grated potato and thyme, like a hash brown and a bread in one.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 2 tbsp oil until no dry patches remain, cover and rest 15 min.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Give four rounds of folds 30 min apart, lifting and laying each side over the middle, until the dough is springy and full of air.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Spread 2 tbsp oil over the tin, add the dough, flip to coat and press out to the corners. Cover and leave about 1 h to puff.

steps.title: Potato
steps.text: Near the end of the rise, coarsely grate the potatoes, gather them in a clean tea towel and wring hard over the sink until no more liquid drips out. Toss with 2 tbsp oil, the thyme, salt and pepper. Dry shreds fry in the oil on top of the bread rather than steaming.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Dimple the dough firmly, then scatter the potato over it in a loose, even layer, leaving a few gaps.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 28-32 min, until the potato is browned and crisp at the tips and the base is golden; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 15 min on a rack and cut into 12.

tips: Squeeze the potato really hard; leftover water stops it crisping.
Grate the potato just before using so it does not turn grey.
Keep the layer loose and thin; packed shreds steam instead of browning.
storage: Best warm on the day. Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days and re-crisp at 200 °C for 6-8 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
